name: PiiClassification
purpose: Schema-level annotation that tags every field as one of PII, PHI, PCI, or public, gating serialization and logging through a central mask.
api_signature:
from enum import Enum
from typing import Protocol, Any, Mapping

class PiiClass(str, Enum):
    PUBLIC = 'public'
    INTERNAL = 'internal'
    PII = 'pii'
    PHI = 'phi'
    PCI = 'pci'

class PiiClassification(Protocol):
    def classify(self, model: type, field: str) -> PiiClass: ...
    def mask(self, obj: Any, audience: str) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
    def audit_leak(self, obj: Any, sink: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Every persisted field MUST carry a PiiClass annotation; fields without one SHALL fail schema registration at import time.
Serializers and log formatters MUST route through mask() before emission; writing a raw object to a sink is FORBIDDEN.
PHI and PCI fields MUST NEVER be emitted to unauthenticated audiences, even masked, unless the field is explicitly PUBLIC.
mask() output for an audience MUST be deterministic so diff tests can assert non-leakage.
Reclassifying a field down the sensitivity ladder (PHI → PII → PUBLIC) MUST require an audit log entry with approver id.
extension_contract: Frameworks register a schema walker that extracts the annotation and plug an AudienceResolver adapter mapping request contexts to audiences. Custom PiiClass values are added by subclassing the enum and registering a mask policy for each new class.

sources.locator: Requirement 3.4 — render PAN unreadable (masking, truncation, hashing)
MP-3 Media Marking; MP-4 Media Storage

why_essential: Without a schema-level classifier, every endpoint re-invents masking and one forgotten field leaks an SSN to a log; one central primitive makes leakage a type error, not a code-review catch.
alternatives_considered: Regex scrubbers on log output — lossy, high false-negative rate, cannot tell PHI from PII.
Per-endpoint DTO mapping by hand — drifts when schema evolves, provides no provable coverage.
Storing raw then redacting at export — still leaks to logs, backups, and replication.
